chapterNote: Chapter 14 is a long string of antithetical proverbs that hold the wise and the fool side by side, sentence after sentence, until the contrast becomes a whole way of seeing the world. Its recurring concern is what a life actually builds or tears down — a house (v.1), a way that looks right but ends in death (v.12), a laughter that hides grief (v.13). Two truths anchor the chapter: that the fear of the LORD is a strong fortress and a fountain of life (vv.26-27), and that righteousness, not raw power, is what truly exalts a nation (v.34). Running underneath is a steady ethic of mercy toward the poor, in whom a person meets his own Maker (vv.21, 31).

1.text: The wise woman builds up her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
1.amp: Every wise woman [chokmot — wisdom personified, here the woman skilled in the art of living] builds [banah — constructs and establishes] her house [bayith — the household, not just the walls]; but folly [ivvelet] pulls it down [haras — demolishes, tears to the ground] with her own hands.
1.notes: banah (H1129) and haras (H2040) are opposites — to build up versus to tear down; bayith (H1004) means the whole household and its future, not merely the dwelling. The tragedy is that the ruin is self-inflicted: 'with her own hands.'. Also tagged: chokmot (H2454), ivvelet (H200).

2.text: He who walks in his uprightness fears the LORD, but the man whose ways are crooked holds Him in contempt.
2.amp: He who walks [halak] in his uprightness [yosher — straightness, what is level and right] fears [yare] the LORD [YHWH]; but the one twisted in his ways [derek] despises [bazah — shows open contempt] Him.
2.notes: yosher (H3476), straightness, and a crooked walk are set as visible evidence of an invisible posture: how a man lives reveals whether he fears or scorns the LORD (H3068). bazah (H959) is contempt — the perverse man's crookedness is not mere weakness but a slight against God Himself. Also tagged: halak (H1980), yare (H3373), derek (H1870).

3.text: In the mouth of the fool is a rod for his own pride, but the lips of the wise will keep them safe.
3.amp: In the mouth [peh] of the fool [evil] is a rod [choter — a shoot or stick, here a switch for the back] of pride [gaavah — haughtiness, arrogance]; but the lips [saphah] of the wise [chakam] will guard [shamar — keep, preserve] them.
3.notes: the fool's proud speech becomes the very rod that beats him — gaavah (H1346), arrogance, lashes back on the one who speaks it. By contrast the careful lips of the chakam (H2450) act as a shamar (H8104), a guard that keeps the speaker out of harm. Also tagged: peh (H6310), evil (H191), choter (H2415), saphah (H8193).

4.text: Where there are no oxen the manger stays clean, but a rich harvest comes by the strength of the ox.
4.amp: Where there are no oxen [eleph] the manger [ebus — the feeding-trough] is clean [bar — empty and tidy]; but much [rob — abundance] increase [tebuah — yield, produce] comes by the strength [koach] of the ox [shor].
4.notes: a homely parable about the cost of fruitfulness: an empty stall is easy to keep, but a barn that produces a harvest will be messy. koach (H3581), strength, must be fed and tolerated; cleanliness without labor yields nothing. Productivity carries inconvenience. Also tagged: eleph (H504), ebus (H18), bar (H1249), rob (H7230), tebuah (H8393), shor (H7794).

5.text: A faithful witness will not deceive, but a false witness breathes out lies.
5.amp: A faithful [emun — trustworthy, reliable] witness [ed] will not lie [kazab]; but a false [sheqer — deceptive] witness pours out [puach — breathes, puffs forth] lies [kazab].
5.notes: emun (H529), faithfulness, and sheqer (H8267), falsehood, are weighed in the courtroom, where a witness holds another's life in his words. puach (H6315) pictures lying as the very breath of the false witness — deceit comes out of him as naturally as exhaling. Also tagged: ed (H5707); the first kazab is H3577, the closing 'lies' the cognate H3576.

6.text: The scoffer hunts for wisdom and never finds it, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
6.amp: A scorner [luts — the mocker who sneers at correction] seeks [baqash — searches, demands] wisdom [chokmah] and finds none; but knowledge [daat] is easy [qalal — light, comes without strain] to the one who understands [biyn — discerns].
6.notes: the luts (H3887) wants wisdom on his own terms and so it eludes him — the very contempt that defines him bars the door. To the humble discerner, daat (H1847) comes light and ready, because he holds the one posture wisdom requires (cf. Prov 9:10). Also tagged: baqash (H1245), chokmah (H2451), qalal (H7043), biyn (H995).

7.text: Get away from a foolish man once you see there is no knowledge on his lips.
7.amp: Go [yalak] from the presence [neged — the face, the company] of a foolish [kesil — dull, stubborn] man [ish], for you will not find on him lips [saphah] of knowledge [daat].
7.notes: the kesil (H3684) is the dense fool who will not learn; the counsel is simply to leave — to remove oneself from his company, since prolonged exposure to empty talk teaches nothing and corrupts much. Also tagged: yalak (H3212), neged (H5048), ish (H376), saphah (H8193), daat (H1847).

8.text: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his own road, but the folly of fools is sheer self-deception.
8.amp: The wisdom [chokmah] of the prudent [arum — shrewd, clear-eyed] is to understand [biyn] his way [derek]; but the folly [ivvelet] of fools [kesil] is deceit [mirmah — treachery, self-fraud].
8.notes: arum (H6175), shrewdness, is here a virtue: the prudent man examines his own road honestly. The fool's folly is mirmah (H4820), deception — and the deepest deception is the one he works on himself, refusing to see where his path leads. Also tagged: chokmah (H2451), biyn (H995), derek (H1870), ivvelet (H200), kesil (H3684).

9.text: Fools laugh off their guilt, but among the upright there is favor.
9.amp: Fools [evil] mock [luts — scoff] at guilt [asham — guilt, the guilt-offering that makes amends]; but among the upright [yashar] there is favor [ratzon — delight, acceptance].
9.notes: evil (H191) fools treat asham (H817), guilt and its remedy, as a joke — they scorn the very idea that sin must be answered for. But ratzon (H7522), favor and acceptance with God and man, settles among the yashar (H3477), who take sin seriously enough to seek atonement. Also tagged: luts (H3887).

10.text: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger can share in its joy.
10.amp: The heart [leb] knows [yada] its own [nephesh — soul, inmost self] bitterness [morah]; and no stranger [zar — an outsider] mingles [arab — intermeddles, enters in] with its joy [simchah].
10.notes: leb (H3820) and nephesh (H5315), heart and soul, name the inner room of a person that no one else fully enters; the deepest griefs and joys are finally private. A zar (H2114), an outsider, cannot truly intermeddle (arab, H6148) in what only the soul itself has tasted. Also tagged: yada (H3045), morah (H4787), simchah (H8057).

11.text: The house of the wicked will be torn down, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
11.amp: The house [bayith] of the wicked [rasha] will be overthrown [shamad — destroyed, wiped out]; but the tent [ohel — the humble dwelling] of the upright [yashar] will flourish [parach — blossom, break into bloom].
11.notes: the proverb reverses appearances: the solid bayith (H1004) of the rasha (H7563) is razed by shamad (H8045), while the flimsy ohel (H168) of the upright parach (H6524) — buds and blooms like a living plant. Permanence belongs not to structure but to righteousness. Also tagged: yashar (H3477).

12.text: There is a way that looks right to a man, but its end is the road to death.
12.amp: There is [yesh] a way [derek] that seems right [yashar — straight] before [panim — in the eyes of] a man [ish]; but its end [acharit — final outcome] is the ways [derek] of death [mavet].
12.notes: the verse turns on irony: a road can look yashar (H3477), perfectly straight to the eye, and still arrive at mavet (H4194), death. acharit (H319), the outcome, not the appearance, is the true test of a path — a warning so weighty Proverbs repeats it verbatim in 16:25. Also tagged: yesh (H3426), derek (H1870), panim (H6440), ish (H376).

13.text: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of such mirth is grief.
13.amp: Even in laughter [sechok] the heart [leb] is in pain [kaab — aches, grieves]; and the end [acharit] of that mirth [simchah] is heaviness [tugah — sorrow, gloom].
13.notes: sechok (H7814), laughter, and kaab (H3510), to ache, sit side by side in the same heart — joy worn on the face can cover a wound underneath. And acharit (H319) again: the merriment that does not rest on God runs out into tugah, heaviness, when the laughter fades. Also tagged: leb (H3820), simchah (H8057), tugah (H8424).

14.text: The backslider in heart gets his fill of his own ways, but a good man is satisfied from what is his.
14.amp: The backslider [sug — the one who turns away, slides back] in heart [leb] will be filled [saba — glutted, given his fill] with his own ways [derek]; and a good [tov] man [ish] is satisfied from himself.
14.notes: the recompense is exact: the one whose heart slides back from God is saba (H7646), filled to the full — with himself, his own derek and nothing more. The tov (H2896) man too reaps from his own life, but his harvest is good. Each eats the fruit of the road he chose. Also tagged: sug (H5472), leb (H3820), derek (H1870), ish (H376).

15.text: The simple believe every word, but the prudent watch where they set their feet.
15.amp: The simple [peti — the naive, easily led] believes [aman — trusts, takes as firm] every word [dabar]; but the prudent [arum] looks well [biyn — considers, discerns] to his step [ashur — his going, his pace].
15.notes: the peti (H6612), open to any voice, swallows every dabar (H1697) whole; the arum (H6175) weighs his ashur (H838), his footing, before he moves. Discernment is not cynicism but care — testing words before trusting them. Also tagged: aman (H539), biyn (H995).

16.text: The wise man fears and turns from evil, but the fool is reckless and sure of himself.
16.amp: A wise [chakam] man fears [yare] and turns aside [sur — departs, removes himself] from evil [ra]; but the fool [kesil] rages on [abar — charges across, oversteps] and is confident [batach — sure, self-assured].
16.notes: holy fear and prudent retreat go together in the chakam (H2450): he yare (H3373), reveres, and so sur (H5493), steps away from harm. The kesil (H3684) does the reverse — he barrels ahead (abar, H5674) in a confidence (batach, H982) that is really only blindness to danger. Also tagged: ra (H7451).

17.text: A man quick to anger acts foolishly, and a schemer is hated.
17.amp: He that is quick [qatsar — short, soon] to anger [aph — the flaring nostril, hot wrath] commits [asah] folly [ivvelet]; and a man [ish] of evil schemes [mezimmah — crafty plots] is hated [sane].
17.notes: two failures of self-mastery: the man short of temper (aph, H639, literally the flaring nose) erupts into ivvelet (H200), folly, in the heat of a moment; the cold schemer turns mezimmah (H4209) — the planning mind — toward harm, and earns the hatred of all. Hot rashness and cold calculation are both condemned. Also tagged: qatsar (H7116), asah (H6213), ish (H376), sane (H8130).

18.text: Folly is the portion the naive fall heir to, while a crown of knowledge encircles the prudent.
18.amp: The simple [peti] inherit [nachal — take as their portion] folly [ivvelet]; but the prudent [arum] are crowned [kathar — encircled, garlanded] with knowledge [daat].
18.notes: what each receives suits what each is: the peti (H6612) comes into folly as a settled inheritance (nachal, H5157), while the arum (H6175) wears daat (H1847) like a crown (kathar, H3803). Folly is the bequest of carelessness; knowledge, the diadem of discernment. Also tagged: ivvelet (H200).

19.text: The evil bow low before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
19.amp: The evil [ra] bow down [shachah — prostrate themselves] before [panim] the good [tov]; and the wicked [rasha] at the gates [shaar — the city gate, the seat of judgment] of the righteous [tsaddiq].
19.notes: the final order is reversed from the present one: those who now scorn the godly will one day shachah (H7817), bow low, before them. That the wicked wait at the shaar (H8179) — the gate where justice was dispensed — pictures their ultimate subjection to the tsaddiq (H6662). Also tagged: ra (H7451), panim (H6440), tov (H2896), rasha (H7563).

20.text: The poor man is shunned even by his neighbor, but the rich have many who love them.
20.amp: The poor [rush — destitute, needy] is hated [sane] even by his own neighbor [rea — friend, companion]; but many [rav] are the lovers [ahab — those who profess love] of the rich [ashir].
20.notes: a hard, observed truth, stated without endorsing it: poverty (rush, H7326) drives even a rea (H7453), a near neighbor, away, while wealth gathers crowds of ahab (H157), 'lovers' — a love drawn by the riches, not the man. The next verse supplies the moral correction this one only describes. Also tagged: sane (H8130), rav (H7227), ashir (H6223).

21.text: Whoever despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is the one who shows kindness to the poor.
21.amp: He who despises [buz — holds in contempt] his neighbor [rea] sins [chata — misses the mark, offends]; but he who is gracious [chanan — shows favor, deals kindly] to the poor [anav — humble, afflicted] — blessed [osher — happy, fortunate] is he.
21.notes: answering v.20, this verse names contempt for a neighbor as chata (H2398), real sin — not mere bad manners. And it pronounces osher (H835), the deep happiness of blessedness, on the one who shows chanan (H2603), grace, to the anav (H6035), the lowly. Mercy to the poor is counted as godliness. Also tagged: buz (H936), rea (H7453).

22.text: Do not those who plot evil go astray? But mercy and truth belong to those who plan good.
22.amp: Do they not err [taah — wander, go astray] who devise [charash — plow, engrave, plot in silence] evil [ra]? But mercy [chesed — steadfast love, loyalty] and truth [emeth — faithfulness, reliability] belong to those who devise [charash] good [tov].
22.notes: charash (H2790), to engrave or plot quietly, is used of both designs — evil and good are each crafted deliberately. Those who carve out evil taah (H8582), lose the way; but chesed and emeth (H2617, H571) — the great covenant pair, steadfast love and faithfulness — attend those who plan good. Also tagged: ra (H7451), tov (H2896).

23.text: In all hard labor there is profit, but mere talk leads only to want.
23.amp: In all labor [etsev — toil, painful effort] there is profit [mothar — advantage, gain]; but the talk [dabar] of the lips [saphah] tends only to want [machsor — lack, poverty].
23.notes: etsev (H6089) is laborious, sweating toil — and it yields mothar (H4195), real gain. But words alone, the dabar of busy saphah (H8193) with no work behind them, run out into machsor (H4270), need. Diligence builds; chatter starves. Also tagged: dabar (H1697).

24.text: The crown of the wise is their riches, but the folly of fools yields only more folly.
24.amp: The crown [atarah — diadem, wreath] of the wise [chakam] is their riches [osher]; but the folly [ivvelet] of fools [kesil] is folly [ivvelet].
24.notes: wisdom adorns itself — the chakam (H2450) wears his fruitfulness like an atarah (H5850), a crown. The fool has no such ornament: turn his folly over and you find only more of the same. ivvelet (H200) repeated drives the point home — folly produces nothing but itself. Also tagged: kesil (H3684); and osher (H6239), riches — a different word from the osher of v.21 (H835), happiness.

25.text: A truthful witness saves lives, but a deceitful one breathes out lies.
25.amp: A true [emeth] witness [ed] delivers [natsal — rescues, snatches from danger] souls [nephesh]; but a deceitful [mirmah — treacherous] witness pours out [puach — breathes forth] lies [kazab].
25.notes: echoing v.5, this verse raises the stakes: honest testimony does not merely avoid wrong but natsal (H5337), actively rescues nephesh (H5315) — lives hang on it in court. The false witness, by contrast, simply exhales mirmah (H4820), treachery, as v.5's liar exhaled deceit. Also tagged: emeth (H571), ed (H5707), puach (H6315), kazab (H3577).

26.text: In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence, and for His children there will be a refuge.
26.amp: In the fear [yirah — reverent awe] of the LORD [YHWH] is strong [oz — mighty] confidence [mivtach — security, a sure trust]; and His children [ben] will have a place of refuge [machseh — shelter, hiding-place].
26.notes: yirah (H3374), the fear of the LORD, is no anxious dread but the ground of oz (H5797), strong security — the very thing the self-confident fool of v.16 only imagines he has. And the blessing runs to the next generation: the ben (H1121), the children of the God-fearer, find a machseh (H4268), a shelter, for themselves. Also tagged: YHWH (H3068), mivtach (H4009).

27.text: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a man away from the snares of death.
27.amp: The fear [yirah] of the LORD [YHWH] is a fountain [maqor — spring, source] of life [chay]; to turn aside [sur — depart] from the snares [moqesh — traps, baited lures] of death [mavet].
27.notes: a companion to v.26: yirah (H3374) is a maqor (H4726), a living spring of chay (H2416) — it does not merely shelter from death but pours out life. And it does the work of v.16 again, leading a man to sur (H5493), turn away, from the moqesh (H4170), the hidden traps, of mavet (cf. Prov 13:14). Also tagged: YHWH (H3068), mavet (H4194).

28.text: A king's glory is in the multitude of his people, but without subjects a prince is ruined.
28.amp: In the multitude [rob — abundance] of people [am — the nation, the populace] is the king's honor [hadarah — glory, majesty]; but in the lack [ephes — nothing, the dwindling away] of people [leom] is the ruin [mechittah — terror, downfall] of the prince [razon].
28.notes: a ruler's true splendor (hadarah, H1927) lies not in treasure or armies but in a thriving am (H5971), a numerous people. Where the population dwindles to ephes (H657), nothing, the prince faces mechittah (H4288), ruin — a king without subjects is no king at all. Also tagged: rob (H7230), leom (H3816), razon (H7333).

29.text: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but the hot-tempered exalts folly.
29.amp: He who is slow [arek — long, patient] to wrath [aph — hot anger] is of great [rav] understanding [tebunah — discernment, insight]; but he who is hasty [qatsar — short] of spirit [ruach] lifts up [rum — exalts, displays] folly [ivvelet].
29.notes: the Hebrew idiom is vivid: the patient man is 'long of nose' (arek aph) and full of tebunah (H8394); the rash man is 'short of spirit' (qatsar ruach) and rum (H7311) — he hoists his folly up like a banner for all to see. Patience and discernment are bound together (cf. Jas 1:19). Also tagged: arek (H750), aph (H639), rav (H7227), qatsar (H7116), ruach (H7307), ivvelet (H200).

30.text: A heart at peace gives life to the body, but envy is rot in the bones.
30.amp: A sound [marpe — healing, tranquil] heart [leb] is the life [chay] of the flesh [basar — the body, the whole physical self]; but envy [qinah — jealousy, consuming zeal] is rottenness [raqab — decay] of the bones [etsem].
30.notes: marpe (H4832) is a healed, tranquil leb (H3820) — and such peace gives chay (H2416) to the very basar (H1320), the body. But qinah (H7068), envious jealousy, works inward like raqab (H7538), rot, eating the etsem (H6106), the bones — the inmost frame. The proverb sees how the soul's state seeps into the flesh.

31.text: Whoever oppresses the poor insults his Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him.
31.amp: He who oppresses [ashaq — exploits, extorts] the poor [dal — the weak, the lowly] reproaches [charaph — taunts, reviles] his Maker [oseh — the One who made him]; but he who is gracious [chanan — shows favor] to the needy [evyon — the destitute] honors [kabad — gives weight, glorifies] Him.
31.notes: to ashaq (H6231) the dal (H1800) is to charaph (H2778), revile, the God who made both rich and poor — the insult passes straight from the victim to his Maker. Conversely, chanan (H2603) toward the evyon (H34) is reckoned as kabad (H3513), honor given to God Himself (cf. Prov 17:5; Matt 25:40). Also tagged: oseh (H6213), the participle of asah, to make.

32.text: The wicked is thrown down by his own evil, but the righteous has refuge even in death.
32.amp: The wicked [rasha] is driven away [dachah — thrust down, shoved out] in his wickedness [ra]; but the righteous [tsaddiq] has refuge [chasah — takes shelter, finds hope] in his death [mavet].
32.notes: the rasha (H7563) is dachah (H1760), thrust down by the very evil he served. But the tsaddiq (H6662) chasah (H2620) — takes refuge, finds hope — even in the face of mavet (H4194); death itself is not bare ruin for him but a sheltering, a hint of hope beyond the grave. Also tagged: ra (H7451).

33.text: Wisdom rests quietly in the heart of the discerning, but among fools it makes itself known.
33.amp: Wisdom [chokmah] rests [nuach — settles, remains at home] in the heart [leb] of him who has understanding [biyn]; but in the midst [qereb — inward parts] of fools [kesil] it is made known [yada — becomes evident].
33.notes: chokmah (H2451) nuach (H5117), comes to rest, finds a settled home in the discerning leb (H3820). The fool has no such inward dwelling: what is in the qereb (H7130) of the kesil (H3684) cannot hide but yada (H3045), shows itself — whatever folly is inside him quickly comes out. Also tagged: biyn (H995).

34.text: Righteousness lifts a nation high, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
34.amp: Righteousness [tsedaqah — right conduct, justice] exalts [rum — lifts up, raises high] a nation [goy]; but sin [chattath — offense, missing the mark] is a reproach [chesed — here in its rare sense of shame, disgrace] to any people [leom].
34.notes: tsedaqah (H6666), moral right-doing, is what rum (H7311), raises a goy (H1471) to true greatness — not wealth, conquest, or size. chattath (H2403), sin, is its undoing: a leom (H3816), a people, is brought low not by weakness but by guilt. A foundational text for a biblical view of national life. Also tagged: chesed (H2617) — the covenant word of v.22, here in its rare inverted sense of reproach.

35.text: A king's favor rests on a servant who acts wisely, but his wrath falls on one who brings shame.
35.amp: The king's favor [ratzon — delight, goodwill] is toward a servant [ebed] who deals wisely [sakal — acts with prudence and success]; but his wrath [ebrah — overflowing fury] is against him who causes shame [bosh — brings disgrace].
35.notes: ratzon (H7522), royal goodwill, falls on the ebed (H5650) who is sakal (H7919) — one who handles his charge with skill and brings it to good end. But the servant who acts so as to bosh (H954), to shame his master, meets ebrah (H5678), a king's overflowing anger. Competence and faithfulness, not flattery, win a wise ruler's favor.
